tldr: Cloudflare’s public-beta Auto Router trades some benchmark performance for a claimed two-thirds cost reduction by choosing a model for each request.
Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, giving PyTorch users a new path to run workloads on Google TPUs.

top.title: Apollo analysis says most companies have yet to see financial returns from AI
top.summary: An Apollo economist says that, despite widespread investment, companies outside the biggest technology firms have seen no financial payoff from AI. The report frames this as a broad finding, but the excerpt provides no underlying figures.
top.why: Use workload-level evidence—not industry hype—to set ROI expectations and decide whether a proposed AI hosting investment is justified.

top.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router picks a model for each request in public beta
top.summary: Cloudflare’s AI Gateway beta scores request complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence to select a model. Cloudflare says its router scores 10 points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at one-third the cost; practitioners question how well it tracks stakes across long agent sessions.
top.why: Evaluate request routing as a way to lower inference costs, but test quality on your own workloads—especially multi-step sessions—before relying on it.

top.title: Google and Meta open-source TorchTPU for native PyTorch on TPUs
top.summary: Google and Meta released TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs; Meta says it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto the hardware. The announcement has renewed questions about TPU availability and vendor lock-in.
top.why: If you are weighing accelerator options, assess whether PyTorch support makes TPU capacity a viable alternative—and how much your design would depend on Google’s hardware.
